title: Refresh agentic workflow template: canonical streaming + tool calling loop (w/ structured output validation)
author: Jean-Paul Laurent
release_notes: Quickstarts: agentic workflow template updated to the canonical streaming event model and tool-calling semantics. Includes robust handling for partial tool arguments during streaming and JSON schema validation/retry guidance for structured output.
description: Summary: This refreshes the agentic workflow quickstart to match the new canonical patterns we’re standardizing across SDKs/docs for (1) streaming deltas/final assembly, (2) tool calling (including partial args while streaming + parallel tool calls), and (3) structured output using JSON schema constraints with validation + retry. Motivation: Support and SE feedback has been consistent that current templates encourage brittle behavior: assuming tool-call args arrive in a single chunk, treating streamed JSON as parseable at every delta, and mixing older message shapes across languages. This template is frequently copy/pasted into production prototypes, so we want it to be the “golden” implementation that matches the refreshed docs. What changed: - Replaced the old stream consumer loops with the canonical event-handling pattern: accumulate assistant text deltas, accumulate tool_call argument deltas by tool_call_id, and only execute tools once a tool_call is finalized; handle errors via a single error branch that logs an actionable hint and exits non-zero. - Updated tool calling to the standard semantics: tools defined once at request time, tool calls emitted by the model, the client executes tools and sends tool_result messages back, repeat until the assistant returns a final response. - Added a structured-output step for the planning phase using a JSON schema; parses only after final message assembly; validates schema; on failure retries once with a “repair” prompt and returns a clear error if still invalid. - Updated README steps to be copy/paste correct, including required env vars, model selection guidance, and expected console output. - Added a smoke test script and CI-friendly flags to run a deterministic “offline” mode using fixtures (so CI doesn’t require live API calls) while still documenting a live mode for users. Template behavior (high-level): 1) User asks a task. 2) Assistant streams a plan in structured output (JSON) matching schema Plan{goal, steps[]}. 3) Agent executes tool calls (example tools: web_search(query), get_page(url), now_iso()). Tool calls may be parallel. 4) Agent streams the final answer with citations produced from tool results. Notes on edge cases handled (addresses SUP-18421 / SUP-18436): - Partial tool args: we buffer tool_call arguments by tool_call_id; we do not JSON.parse until the tool_call is marked complete. If the model sends malformed args, we surface a clear error including the partial buffer and a hint to try the recommended model(s). - Structured output JSON parse errors: we only parse after final assembly; validation uses a strict schema; retry path prompts the model to emit only valid JSON (no prose) and includes the validation error message. Repos/areas impacted (high level): - templates/agentic-workflow/{node,python,go}/ updated - docs/README updates for env vars and run steps - fixtures/ added for offline smoke tests Key files (high-level): - templates/agentic-workflow/node/src/agent.ts (canonical stream loop + tool execution loop) - templates/agentic-workflow/python/agent.py (buffered tool args + structured output validation) - templates/agentic-workflow/go/agent/main.go (stream event switch + helper for final message assembly) - templates/agentic-workflow/README.md (copy/paste instructions + expected output) - scripts/smoke/agentic_workflow_smoke.sh (offline fixture mode + optional live mode) Commits (squashed): 1) agentic-workflow: replace legacy streaming with canonical event handling 2) agentic-workflow: tool calling loop + parallel tool calls example 3) agentic-workflow: structured output schema + validate/repair retry 4) quickstart README: env vars, model notes, expected output 5) smoke: add offline fixtures + smoke runner Notes for reviewers: - Please sanity-check that the event naming and tool result message shape match the current SDK docs conventions (see linked Linear). - Ensure we don’t imply guarantees we can’t make across models; this template defaults to a recommended model but includes a fallback note. Smoke test notes: - Offline: ./scripts/smoke/agentic_workflow_smoke.sh --offline (uses fixtures to validate stream assembly + tool-call buffering + schema validation paths) - Live (optional): REDWOOD_API_KEY=... ./scripts/smoke/agentic_workflow_smoke.sh --live --model redwood/verified-agentic (prints a short transcript; assertions are lenient to avoid flake). CI: - quickstarts-lint: PASS - node-build: PASS - python-lint: PASS - go-test: PASS - smoke-offline: PASS Review conversation highlights: - Ibrahim Khan: Requested that we explicitly demonstrate buffering tool args until completion and not parsing during deltas; also asked to align event names in comments with the streaming conventions doc. Addressed in commit 2 and comment pass in commit 1. - Dana Lo: Requested TypeScript example avoid any SDK-internal types; ensured the sample compiles under strict mode and uses runtime guards for event variants. Updated agent.ts accordingly. - Wei Chen: Requested README language changes to match docs terminology (“structured output” vs “JSON mode”) and a short callout about model variability. Updated README and added a note about retry/repair. - Leila Farouk: Requested that smoke test offline fixtures cover the partial tool args case and a structured-output invalid JSON case. Added two fixtures and assertions; wired into smoke-offline job. Outcome: Merged (squash) after approvals and green CI.
